verdict.rationale: GitCafe's repository rulesets can require pull requests, reviews, code-owner approval and passing checks before merging, with an Evaluate mode that only warns so rules can be trialled first. Checks come from Buildkite builds and GitHub Actions results, but the evidence does not show how teams define arbitrary custom quality or compliance checks, so coverage is partial. missing for 10: documented support for arbitrary custom checks (e.g. a commit-status/checks API for third-party tools), org-wide enforcement of compliance policies, independent or hands-on corroboration that required checks block merges.

support.subject: As a devops-lead, I can enforce custom quality and compliance merge checks on pull requests

citations.quote: A ruleset protects matching branches or tags: it can require pull requests, reviews and passing checks, or block deletion and force pushes.
each changed path needs approval from one of its owners in `CODEOWNERS`
the rules only produce warnings, so you can try them first.
GitCafe shows Buildkite builds on a repository's **CI** tab and as checks on pull requests.
GitHub Actions results arrive as checks.
